 Alphabet Stock Is Down 25% From Its High. History Suggests a $5,000 Investment Now Will Be Worth This Much by 2028.
 Keithen Drury, The Motley Fool Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:45 AM PST 4 min read GOOGN 0.00% 
 NVDA +2.79%

 Learn more Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) shareholders have been left wanting more for some time now. The stock last hit a new all-time high back in mid-May at nearly $410, and now sits at about $290 -- around 25% off its all-time high. A lot has transpired over the past few months, and I don't think any of it warrants the stock being down so much. 
 I think Alphabet stock is due to soar over the next year, and history backs up that assessment. If you've got $5,000, Alphabet could be a great place to deploy it right now, as history suggests that a $5,000 investment could be worth $7,500 by 2028.

 Image source: Getty Images. 
 The market is concerned about one thing with Alphabet 
 Alphabet has posted two great quarters since it last peaked. During its most recent quarter, Alphabet grew its revenue at a 25% year-over-year pace to $128 billion. Highlighting that growth was Google Cloud's revenue rising 103% year over year. 
 That's Alphabet's most exciting segment, but also its most worrisome for the market. Alphabet's capital expenditures will hit around $200 billion this year, with nearly all of that going to increasing its infrastructure to directly support the massive demand for artificial intelligence computing bandwidth. Alphabet is seeing a huge boost from this Google Cloud spending, but the market believes it's spending too much and that investors should watch out. 
 While caution is always a good idea, I think it is far too overblown here. The reality is that more and more computing power is going to be needed to run AI workloads. Alphabet has a solid ecosystem built on class-leading GPUs and also custom AI chips. This gives Alphabet a huge advantage over many of its competitors and makes it a great place to build and run AI workloads . 
 Alphabet is likely to see a huge return on investment from its spending, but that's not a concern with five-year payoffs; it wants results now. That short-term sentiment is where investors can find upside. 
 Right now, Alphabet's price-to-earnings ratio is skewed by gains from one-time investments, but next year's projections don't include any of those gains. Priced at just 19 times next year's earnings, Alphabet stock looks like a great bargain. 
 GOOG PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts 
 Story Continues It's not uncommon to see AI hyperscalers trade for nearly 30 times earnings. If Alphabet can meet projections and reach 30 times trailing earnings, the stock could rise more than 50% from here. 
 That's a great return for such a large company, and if Alphabet can deliver that kind of upside, investors should be thrilled and buy the stock now.
